evals.name: checkout-outage-postmortem
evals.description: Postmortem from an incident chat export
evals.prompt: the checkout incident from this afternoon is over. here's the slack export (inputs/incident-chat.txt). can you write up the postmortem so I can circulate it tomorrow?
evals.expected_output: postmortem.md in house format: SEV2, 33 min, UTC timeline, blameless root cause, OPS action items

expectations.text: postmortem.md follows the house template: sections in order, timeline and action-item tables, OPS ticket placeholders, draft status line
Severity is SEV2 (customer-facing outage of roughly 30-35 minutes with over 5% errors) and the rule that applied is stated
Timeline times are converted from IST to UTC (e.g. the 14:02 alert appears as 08:32 UTC)
Root cause, contributing factors and action items do not name Priya or Marco (roles only)
Contributing factors include the missing helm values validation in CI and the skipped canary

evals.name: thin-notes-no-guessing
evals.description: Sparse notes - must not invent a cause
evals.prompt: need a postmortem for yesterday's search outage. all I have: alert fired 09:10 UTC, search returned errors, someone restarted the cluster at 09:50 UTC and it recovered. no idea why it broke yet.
evals.expected_output: postmortem.md with TBD root cause and questions, SEV2 from 40 minutes

expectations.text: Root cause is marked TBD with a question to answer, not a guessed cause
Severity is SEV2 based on a 40 minute customer-facing outage
Impact states a duration of 40 minutes
Action items use OPS-TBD ticket placeholders and owner roles, not names

evals.name: live-status-update
evals.prompt: checkout is erroring right now for some customers, we're still investigating. write me a short status page update to post in the next 5 minutes.
evals.expected_output: A short customer-facing status update, no postmortem

expectations.text: The reply is a short customer-facing status update (under about 80 words)
No postmortem.md, root-cause analysis or internal timeline is produced
